item.title: The Electrical Girl
item.description: A 14 year old girl who has electrical powers
item.content:encoded:
Special Containment Procedures:

SCP-5127 is kept in site 19 and to be kept in a 15 by15 meter room guarded by two guards out side of the container to avoid containment breach.

There are to be two back up generators within 100 meters of SCP-5127’s containment. No SCP’s are allowed within 150 meters of SCP-5127 including any unauthorized personnel (Class D is allowed for testing).

All guards guarding SCP-5127 are to be striped of any electrical equipment and are to put the equipment in a steel box out side of the 100 meter parameters.

SCP-5127 is to have entertainment at all times to avoid boredom which unconsciously causes a electromagnetic pulse which can cause a containment breach.

Description:
SCP-5127 is what appears to be a fourteen year old girl who has the ability to cause lethal electromagnetic pulses uncontrollably this is prevented by SCP-5127 having entertainment to prevent boredom. SCP-5127 also has a defense mechanism in which (if pierced by metal) causes an electrical shock killing the holder of the metal (see incident 5127-1) SCP-5127 immediately feels guilt after death of personnel except Class D personnel. Researchers assigned to SCP-5127 noted SCP-5127 is aware of Class D’s actions and knows there in the foundation as testing for a reason

item.title: Malicious Magnet (seeking greenlights)
item.description: A floating, anomalous magnetic object
item.content:encoded:
A floating, anomalous magnetic object that works like a normal magnet, except it has the ability to cause as much harm to humans as possible.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Similar to a standard SCP article, having 4 additional addendums that show testing logs.

Elevator Pitch: A floating, inanimate, red metal object that exhibits an anomalous magnetic force. It will work as a normal magnet when presented with most metal objects. However, it will alter its magnetic force when humans are around, causing pain (due to altering blood flow) or even death to individuals with things like pacemakers or prosthetic replacements. It will also destroy any technology that comes close enough using this force.

Central Narrative: The SCP was originally found in a meteoroid crash site. The anomaly was originally reported to the foundation because of the death of 3 individuals investigating the meteorite. It was relatively difficult to retrieve because it had torn the body armor of the MTF sent to investigate, causing major injuries to the chest area. It was eventually retrieved aircraft, towing it to containment through a long-distance hook.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think this SCP has the potential for a lot of interesting testing and theorizing, and I don't think a sentient magnet concept has been done before.

Additional Notes: It is unknown if this SCP is sentient or not.

item.title: Alternate dimension where man-made flight is nearly impossible
item.description: This dimension is almost exactly the same as ours, except humans cannot go above a certain height limit in the atmosphere without going insane or catatonic.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Science Fiction, Religion

Page Layout: There will be a series of interviews, documenting what the alternate universe is like, followed by an addendum showing how certain historical events have changed due to airplanes not being in wide use, and a final addendum that reveals its a world where God has deemed that humans are not allowed to leave the planet.

Elevator Pitch: This is an alternate dimension where man-made flight is essentially impossible, due to a phenomenon that occurs above a certain altitude (current thinking is about 6km up) that makes piloting and generally thinking rationally impossible.

Central Narrative: The story will show how the Foundations of both universes try to work together to discover the cause of the anomaly, as well as discover the differences in each other's histories.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Much of the history of the 20th's century was shaped by the advent of air power. But what if air power was never a thing? Air craft carriers, strategic bombing, mail by air, even tourism would all completely change. This SCP will examine ways such a world might work.

Additional Notes: I've had this idea for a couple of years now, but I was never sure what to do with it. Recently, I remembered that there's a verse in the Quran that says:

"O assembly of jinns and men! If you have power to pass beyond the zones of the heavens and the earth, then pass (them)! But you will never be able to pass them, except with authority (from Allah)!"

Essentially, the cause is that in our world, God has allowed humanity to leave the heavens and earth, but in SCP-X, God has not allowed this.

item.title: Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome
item.description: An anomalous version of Impostor Syndrome that causes the person to conspire against themselves.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Personal horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous variation of Impostor Syndrome in which the affected person believes they are an actual impostor, stealing their own memories and identity. Severe cases might end up in the subject trying to kill themselves in an attempt at returning things to their right way.

Central Narrative: An up-and-coming Foundation researcher starts to conspire against themself, to the point of hiring a hitman to kill themself. This catches the attention of the psychiatric department and an investigation begins.
After several therapy sessions the affected researcher is put through a brain scan and the anomaly is found: it is an auto immune response to the constant contact the reaearcher had had with memetic and antimemetic material. It caused their brain to stop recognizing their own memories.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
· An anomalous twist to an everyday problem, the Impostor Syndrome, a condition that causes a person to question their skills and value
· The concept of a memetic disease and a memetic immune system and how these interact with other memetic SCP articles and tales
· Potential long term characters and concepts to be used and explored by other articles and authors

Additional Notes: I haven't started writing it yet, this is the very first concept of my very first SCP article so I am open to all critics and suggestions :)

item.title: it's all in your head (seeking greenlight)
item.description: a somewhat sentient parasite that controls the human mind and uses it to encourage others to get themselves infected
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Parasite enters the brain of a human and latches onto certain parts of it encouraging it or forcing it to meet its demands. The parasite spreads via bodily contact with its nesting spot or anybody infected. nesting spots are found within contaminated areas such as sewers, heavily polluted bodies of water. the parasite eventually makes its host practically braindead only able to meet the demands of its master, while the parasite uses the body as a vessel to transmit the parasite and as a food source. the parasite also uses any forms of mental illness and traumatic moments, fond memories, anything that it can find inside the host's mind to exploit.

the parasite uses the researcher to create a document on the parasite claiming that it's not dangerous and that it is beneficial. while writing it, however, consciousness snaps back and he realizes what he is writing and tries to correct it, but with the parasite still in control of his mind, he fails.

Central Narrative: I intend on creating an article that tries to encourage you that the parasite is completely harmless while subtlely explaining what it actually does, while its host tries to fight it off, to no avail

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the parasite is using humans as hosts to try to encourage others to get themselves infected, specifically via the article

Additional Notes: I would like as much critique as I can get.

item.title: Press "A" to Jump
item.description: A character that appears in the background of video games, corrupting it enough to drag the player into the distorted and horrific game.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): standard layout. Special Containment Procedures, description, discovery log and testing logs

Elevator Pitch:
basic idea is, there is a character that appears in video games and corrupts the game every time the player fails or loses a level/life. once corrupted enough, the character appears in the foreground and grabs the player through the screen. trapping them in the corrupted game.

Central Narrative:
The scp foundation finds this SCP by going to a POI's last known position. Who claimed to be part of GAW (gamers against weed). when they find his place one of the agents turns on a TV and is pulled into a game. After some time an old game cartridge is found, after testing it though, it is found that any video game that comes within a 200-300 meter radius of the cartridge becomes infected and slowly turns into an instance of the SCP, going through 5 stages of infection before the player is pulled in. all while the player is experiencing an addiction to complete the game.(even if previously completed)

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
this SCP is unique in the sense that people will fear dying, pausing or leaving a video incomplete. which many people do IRL, giving more spooks, the people trapped inside will still be alive and suffering in a corrupt, horrific and incompatible game. only being able to communicate when some one plays the game. (games would be safe to play after an abduction event).

Additional Notes:
second try at an SCP. hope this idea is better.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Green Man's Chefs (Edited and revised)
item.description: A mysterious restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in 19XX. The building was then contained by the Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Green Man's chefs are green faceless humanoids wearing a chef's attire.
  • They are sentient and are capable of speech despite without having a mouth.
  • No one knows where the kitchen is. The chefs are the only ones that know.
  • They are friendly to humans and would love to talk with them.
  • When being asked anything about their kitchen, they'll become agitated and reply with "no".

Central Narrative: In 19XX, a restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in Alaska. The customers said that they've never seen the kitchen nor any door leading to it but said that the chefs there were friendly. Their menu was constantly changing and it never said what dish it was. All it said was something like "Order #01", "Order #02", and so on.

The Foundation then secured the restaurant and sent in agents to order food and report back on what they were served. Or at least, what they think they were served. An agent stated that he ate a salad that only had lettuce but still tastes like a salad even with the only ingredient being lettuce. The agent said that it was the greatest salad he tasted. The agent brought some of the lettuce leaves with him. The lettuce was examined. The lettuce was made of an unidentified substance mixed with a highly radioactive substance.

One report from an agent stated he was wandering around the restaurant when he found a hallway. He went in and saw a door. But, as he was about to open the door, the agent experienced extreme paranoia and ran away. The agent said that he felt that there was a voice warning him not to come in. Every step he took closer to the door, the voice became louder. He was told to go back to the hallway he found but he refused. Then, it was assumed that the door led to the kitchen.

More agents were sent into the restaurant to find the hallway. No one found it and they returned to the entrance of the restaurant. But, 2 agents weren't present. After a couple of minutes, one of the agents was found. He was shaking in fear. The agent was asked on what happened. He said that he and the other agent found the door. They both went in despite the voice telling them not to come in. What the agent saw was terrifying. The second agent was then stabbed by one of the chefs and the agent managed to run away. Just when the agent was about to say what was the terrifying thing he saw, a chef appeared and ran towards the agent. The chef started to repeatedly stab him while [REDACTED]. More chefs appeared and they carried the agent's remains. The other chefs became aggressive to the other agents. The chefs chased all of them out of the restaurant. After the team managed to exit the restaurant, a closed sign appeared outside the door. The sign read "CLOSED. We are making adjustments to give you the best service we can offer".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: These entities can cook delicious food with unknown ingredients. Who knows what these are and how they get them. The kitchen was never seen so it remains a mystery on how these entities make the food.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP. So, it might be messy or not good.
Edit: Made some changes…

item.title: The Three Sided Coin
item.description: A coin that turns men into monsters, figuratively and literally.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article and Tales

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Standard SCP layout, Wild West layout (think Aces and Eights style) for first tale.

Elevator Pitch

  • Its an anomalous coin that will reveal 3 different sides when flipped over. The 3rd side is anomalous.
  • When the coin lands on the 3rd side it transforms whoever flipped it into a monster.
  • In addition if someone keeps the coin for a long time it will alter their behavior, making them kinda crazy but in a fun way.

Central Narrative: The coins most interesting part isn't the monster but more so what it does to the people in possession of it. It makes them more exuberant, more fond of games and gambling, risk, chaos, but not necessarily evil. Its like the coin makes whoever is holding it chaotic neutral,
but they just happen to have a chaotic evil toy in their pocket, so they're dangerous. The tales will focused less on the coin itself but more on the people its effecting.

Hook: The characters. The concept can be used pretty easily to create stories. The idea that this coin is just floating around and anybody can have it allows people to come up with their own interpretation of how the coin might corrupt someone. Plus the monster is pretty badass too in my opinion.

Notes: I have a draft tale and a rudimentary scp article already written if anyone is interested is seeing them let me know.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Epstein didn't kill himself
item.description: The surveillance footage from Epstein's cell is anti-memetic
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Modern events

+ show block
– hide block

Page Layout (Optional):

Special Containment Procedures: A copy of the scp is kept on hard drive kept in safe.

Description: Video is antimemetic. Foundation wants to know what happened in the video because Epstein was already on their radar for potential ties to a redacted GOI. Research with dangerous z-class mnestics was recently authorized

Document #XXXX-01: letter of authorization

Document #XXXX-02: Report on research with z class mnestics sent to O5. Contains test log with dialogue. Reveals that Epstein was murdered.

Document #XXXX-03: Internal document from O5 council. They believe that it was MC&D. Now they want to use that info to the advantage of the foundation.

Elevator Pitch: The surveillance feed of Epstein's death is anti-memetic. The SCP foundation wants to uncover the mystery of what happened as well as why it was covered up.

Central Narrative: Starting with the Description, I'm going to build a sense of an imposing conspiracy regarding Epstein's death. I will do this by hinting that Epstein was already on the Foundation's radar for being tied to a redacted GOI. I'm going to then hype up the efficacy of z-class mnestics by having their usage require authorization from the O5 council. Using Z-class mnestics as a benchmark, I'm gonna emphasize how extremely anti-memetic the footage. However, the testing will ultimately pull through and reveal that Epstein was murdered. Finally, in a post climax reveal, an internal document from the O5 council will reveal who they bbelieve murdered Epstein, tying back to the redacted GOI from earlier: Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP focuses on modern conspiracies that I imagine everyone on the SCP wiki are familiar with (and maybe even buy into).

Additional Notes: I know that writing an article about Epstein requires care. If I make things to political, I can drive out half of the readers. I also have to make sure remain respectful to his victims. I'm aware of that responsibility and I won't post an article unless I'm confident that I satisfy both of those benchmarks.

item.title: Old-Styled Televisions?
item.description: I'm looking for a specific television model to use for my scp.

item.title: The Man Who Snorts Video Games, Books and Movies Like Cocaine
item.description: A cokehead decides to snort more than just cocaine...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: I have no clue

Elevator Pitch:

  • A cokehead grows ashamed of himself one day and decided to smash a few of his video games. He gets the bright idea to snort the fragments and discovers that doing so gives him a signifcantly weaker version of the main character's powers/skills/abilities/etc.
  • Example: snorting Super Mario Bros lets him jump 18 feet in the air. The catch? He'll break his ankles when he lands.
+What the heck did I just write...?
-Uhh....

Central Narrative:

  • After spending much of his life disappointing his family, friends and divorced spouse, he goes on a downward spiral and then discovers his anomalous ability.
  • At first, he tries to do good.
  • He tries to help an old lady cross the road by snorting Super Mario Bros, picking her up and jumping across the street. It doesn't end well.
  • Then he snorts Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and gets the Master Sword. He attempts to stop a bank robbery. However, he has no formal sword training and ends up dropping it, firing the Master Sword energy beam and accidentally killing someone's dog. The robbers then kick his ass and leave.
  • He finally decides to go down the road of villainy instead.
  • He snorts a copy of Megaman and tries to rob a bank. He ends up burning his hand off because it turns out human flesh isn't made to rapid fire concentrated plasma shots.
  • The Foundation finally notices him and tries to contain him.
  • He snorts a copy of Grand Theft Auto and tries to steal a car.
  • Well, he steals a car, alright.
  • He can't drive and ends up crashing into a fire hydrant.
  • The Foundation catch up to him.
  • Turns out, he kept a secret weapon all him all along; it's a little glass vial filled with fragments of a copy of Persona 5. He snorts it, magically dons a really beat up, low quality edgy black trenchcoat that smells like it hasn't been washed since Persona 1's release date.
  • He tries to summon Arsene and all he gets is a floating top hat that fires a tiny glob of darkness. All it does it make the Foundation Agent sneeze.
  • He gets contained.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Um. Well. He snorts things.

Additional Notes:

Possible copyright issues? I forgot to give a movie and book as an example. Oh well.

item.title: Amateur wizards and how to contain them
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedures, then description of the scp’s and finally interviews addendums and what the foundations future with the scp may hold

Elevator Pitch: A young man found by the foundation with limited knowledge of most anomalies involving, or labeled as magic. A modern day architect can’t explain exactly how the great pyramids were built, but can gain a basic understanding by examining them, and probably come up with a Rough theory. This scp can do the same with magical/ mythical items. As well as use any gained knowledge to concoct his own as he puts it amateur level anomalies ( can’t go into to much detail without making this to long)

Central Narrative:The article shows there interest in his ability to understand the anomalous effects of certain scps, But also the danger he can pose to himself and some people around him, due to his lack of expertise or a mentor. Containment procedures start off easy as they get to know him. But as they realize just how powerful he is the foundation gets stricter and stricter. Finally getting to foam padded rooms, and masks to prevent him from performing magic without heavy supervision. The article will also include the foundations extreme concern of the scp landing in unwanted hands due to its ability to make small scale anomalies.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The scp’s complete immaturity and lack of expertise or knowledge of just how powerful he can be, make him extremely hard to utilize in any situation. But his ability to gain an understanding on certain anomalies make him extremely useful to the foundation. If they can just keep a 14 year old “amateur witch” as he often labels himself: under control

Additional Notes: I am extremely worried about this scp being to overpowered or lacking in restriction. So if that does come up please tell me how to fix it. This whole scp is themed around a witch that’s to young to fully understand what there doing so I was thinking of adding a cat like scp companion. ( this idea will most likely be scrapped due to the already difficult task of polishing the main idea). This is my very first concept so I am fully expecting it to go down in flames and I’m perfectly content with that

An event in which an individual, usually that suffers from sleep paralysis, will experience a dissociative episode(out of body experience), entering someone else's body, the individual suffering the dissociative event will be unable to control the body of the person it is in, the individual will then see an entity stalking the person, which will be oblivious to said entity. item.title: The Most Annoying Fly You'll Ever Meet.
item.description: You know that fly that always seems to sneak its way into your room at night? Well, it can be much, much worse.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror with a tinge of dark comedy.

Page Layout (Optional): A standard SCP article included with experiences of D-Class dealing with the SCP and footnotes of some unusual instances of the SCP

Elevator Pitch: The first instance of SCP-??? is a small gnat that appears in the affected individual’s room anywhere from 10 P.M to 2 A.M and is first seen flying around a light source in the room or heard buzzing past the individual’s ear. This gnat proves extremely annoying, being nearly impossible to catch and contain for the night and will buzz by the individual’s ear just as they’re falling asleep. However, the gnat is very easy to kill, seemingly stopping if it’s approached with the intent of swatting it. But, killing the gnat will activate the next “stage” of SCP-???, this time a fly. Killing this instance again “ramps” up the SCP to a mosquito the next night, and so on and so on until you get mosquitoes with malaria, murder hornets, and other terrible crawlies. However, no matter what stage you’re on, they all follow the same rule of the insect being able to fly around and of being easy to kill but nearly impossible to catch and contain.

Central Narrative: I want to focus on how D-Class subjects either cope or go insane from this terrible predicament, and how bad it can get if you keep ramping up the stages.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A crawly in your rooms at night is something we’ve all dealt with at some point, so I feel like that familiar premise combined with my unique (hopefully) idea activates that deep fear of insects in the reader.

Additional Notes: I’m not positive if I want to have it ramp up to the point of being unbearable, or plateau at a certain point so it’s not enough to be completely devastating, but the annoyance is enough to slowly eat away at the individual. Curious on what your thoughts are.

item.title: Of sirens and memetic agents
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Romance, History

Elevator Pitch: A siren that travels the world's seas in search of someone to marry. She exposes people to auditory and visual memetic agents that will make the exposed person fall in love with her; this usually ends with the siren accidentally drowning the exposed person. Any accurate depiction of her also carries this effect. However, the memes will only work on people who identify as a woman: people who identify as male will have a violent reaction to memes. The memes aren't distributed by artistic interpretations of her.

She first appeared in 1882; she was less of a problem then because she mostly isolated herself in the middle of the Atlantic ocean, not aware of the outside world. However, with the rise of mass media and the internet, she became more of a problem to secrecy as she began patrolling closer to large population centers and started placing advertisements carrying memetic agents on the internet through anomalous and non-anomalous means.

Central Narrative: The foundation originally discovered the siren in 1882, but due to her remote location, the foundation maneuvered ships away from her position and kept her mostly uncontained. The disappearance of Natalie Wood is the first real sign that the Siren has taken more provocative actions to secure a bride. The foundation can get a hold of her and does some interviews:

  • The first goes in-depth about her history: Her familial line is dying off and she was forced into marriage. However, due to her sexuality and her failing relationship with her husband, she ran away from home in search of another bride.
  • The second has the foundation propose an alternative; she can find a bride within the foundation staff as long as she stops advertising on the internet.
  • The third is a list of multiple proposed brides, equipped with memetic dampeners, and the siren's reaction to them. One of them gets selected, and some conversations are logged. It ends on a sweet tone, the siren finally having found someone who likes her back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a wholesome article and this is mostly targeted at an audience that likes that, and it's pretty big. It also plays with the siren formula and introduces it to a modern setting. You could see it as a more family-friendly version of the original ''teenage succubus'' SCP.

page type tale

genre: horror

page layout a transcript of a conversation with passages from the book revelations used as a framing device

Elevator pitch: Going off of what was established in the tale "new job". A former researcher on his death bed shares visions of an apocalyptic battle between SCP-999 and the scarlet king.

central narrative: while being read his last rites, the dying man interrupts the priest and starts yelling about his visions. The priest tries to tell him to save his strength, but the man insists he must listen. The visions begin with a great war between the SCP foundation and 6 other groups of interests, the war being about weather to destroy anomalies, study them, or let them be. The War comes to a head with an all out seige on site 19, where SCP-988 is being kept. During the battle, SCP-999 supposedly dies to save a researcher from SCP-049. That researcher then finds and opens SCP-988 The visions then skip ahead to the end of the seige, where SCP-053 and 682 are united and release some of the most dangerous SCPs. The survivors of the ensuing chaos come together despite their differences to try and stop this army of SCPs, and the Scarlet king feeds off the chaos of this battle. Pretty soon a portal to the scarlet king's world rips open and fire rains down as the Scarlet king enters our world. Just then SCP-999 reappears with a handful of other thaumiel class SCPs. Unfortunately the man dies before he can tell the man how it ends, but he does leave him with a warning not to "face the light when the day comes" before passing away.

hook: its an end of the world prediction that sorta lines up with the book of revelations.

item.title: A (Real) Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
Hi,

I'm planning on writing a meta SCP article on the McCollough effect. Thing is, I suppose you could say this is a real-life cognitohazard. Viewing the images can alter the way your brain perceives colour, causing long-lasting changes to colour perception. In some cases, the effects have lasted months after initial viewing.

I could totally do this… there are McCollough images that are CC compliant. Thing is, this could affect people in real life. I guess I would need some sort of disclaimer warning the reader of the image, but people are just going to assume the warning is fictional. It's not, and these images can alter you in real life.

I don't know how to write a disclaimer that will properly inform the reader of the potential repercussions whilst not breaking the tone of the site.

item.title: The Blur *Seeking Greenlights*
item.description: an SCP article about a mysterious shadow
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is as the name suggest, a blur or as also seen as a shadow. It inhabits the very south of Argentina, the being is observed to have human level or higher intelligence and exhibits some anomalous abilities.

Central Narrative: This SCP is on close watch by the foundation, it having no physical body and only appearing as a semi transparent blur or a shadow makes it impossible to contain. So the foundation has decided to watch it via satellite. While it is not hostile towards anything, it has been observed to kill plant based life around it, likely by an unconscious ability to soak moisture from its surroundings. The foundation has no clear hypothesis for its existence but the most widely accepted one is that the SCP is an alternate dimensional being that exist on a semi 4 dimensional level, allowing it to have no physical body, yet still visible to 3 dimensional beings, although this theory is not proven.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP here has a lot of mystery around it, and I want to be able to not have a definitive answer what it exactly is. While the article will be mostly field notes by observers, I also want to explain why this SCP is as smart as a human and what ties it has to earth.

Additional Notes: I cant really explain everything here but if I can obtain 2 greenlights and make a sandbox, I can go into much better detail about this SCP and why it exist. Im not entirely sure where I can improve the central narrative to make it sound more interesting, but I have many ideas for this SCP so shoot your criticism at me so I can make this sound even more like a true SCP

item.title: The Abyss is Safe (seeking Crits and Greenlight)
item.description: an interdimensional, aquatic SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, and a narrative inter spliced with exploration logs and journal entries

Elevator Pitch: Life came from the cold, dark crushing depths of the sea, and that is where it is most safe, supposedly

Central Narrative: Talassaphobia is the fear of deep ocean, and is super common, but at the same time the ocean is considered to be the origin of all life. This SCP concept takes it to a new level: that beneath the deepest oceanic point on earth, the world is connected to a vast, interdimensional ocean. This ocean/SCP holds no deadly anomalies and living things entering this ocean go into a catatonic state and cannot be hurt or killed. The article would explore strange, normal animals that have entered and been affected by the space's effects, as well as exploration of the space itself. The main narrative doesn't exactly focus on it being this big inter dimensional space though, and is more about the small team of researchers that are for the most part left alone researching it. Along the ideas of “if you stare long enough into the abyss…” theming. While the main SCP may seem big, it is really more about how the people left alone with what would be consider a “safe” sort of anomaly do their best not to lose themselves in it, and what happens to the things that fail.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP takes a common fear and twists it into something welcoming. If you're familiar with the abyss from Dark Souls its similar: more of the pitch black being the true, calm nature of life and less so the rampaging monsters. It expires isolation, survival, and twisting the notion of what the deep ocean is like.

item.title: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious

At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in some apartment in Iran.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Elevator Pitch: At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in an abandoned apartment in Iran.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation is compelled to visit an apartment that everybody, including other agencies concerned with the anomalous, seemed to know about. It turns out that the anomaly is not the apartment itself, but a bonsai tree sitting in the bedroom. The Foundation takes over the entire apartment complex, "managing" it to keep appearances. The apartment, officially the containment cell for the anomaly, looked to be lived in, but beyond writings and personal belongings of the tenant, there are no records of residence.

+ show block
– hide block

They find out that the bonsai tree emits radio signals through an invisible root system throughout the Earth. These radio signals cause those exposed to them for prolonged periods to feel intense dread and regret. Not much else learned about the bonsai tree, and the former tenant is still at large.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Knowledge of an object suddenly enters the collective unconscious.

Additional Notes: What I really want to highlight is the juxtaposition between the ubiquity of the bonsai tree within the collective unconscious and the anonymity of the original tenant. In summary, the tree is supposed to be representative of a universal dread, while the tenant, seemingly untrackable, is like an unobtainable goal.

While drafting this idea, I kept having trouble with suggesting the meaning of the tree's radio signals and the significance of the date in which it manifested. The idea is that the tree sort of feeds off of people's anxieties, and the "root system" connects to the minds of every person on Earth. The problem is that I don't want to be overt about it.

I'm not looking to write something scary or unsettling. I just want to make something that's curious.

item.description: The story of researchers researching other researchers.
item.content:encoded:
The story of researchers researching other researchers. When the lines between 'tester' and 'testee' become blurred.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Page Layout (Optional): It will begin with a standard SCP article structure, followed by a series of experiment logs, journal extracts and Foundation documents explaining the story of the discovery of the subject.

Elevator Pitch: One day a researcher discovers a strange correlation between co-worker drinking a specific brand of soda and disasters/containment breaches occuring to their projects which he is certain is a viable "warning-light" to help contain dangerous SCPs.

Central Narrative: An anonomous researcher in one of the foundation sites has been secretly classified as a thaumiel class SCP, used as an early warning system for potential disasters that may befall foundation projects. Should this researcher drink a can of soda of a brand they typically claim to hate, it is a sign that a project which the researcher is assigned to will have a some form of disaster occur to it.

+ show block
– hide block

One observant co-worker, Dr. Gables, notices this trend and begins documenting it. What follows is a series of test logs and journal extracts of Dr. Gables investigating this anomouly and putting the paperwork in to give the researcher an official SCP designation. As the logs go on, experiments ramp up and start getting strange. By the time Dr. Gables has orchestrated an entire breach event resulting in multiple deaths, we realise that he had been operating without foundation clearance the entire time.

He uses an edited version of his obervations (with his involvment having been removed) to get the researcher an official SCP designation. Following a few more experiments, Dr. Gables goes insane and assaults the researcher. Following this, the Foundation investigates Dr. Gables to find his original observations that proved his involvement in multiple incidents, as well as numorous logs documenting other Foundation personnel and a large amount of blackmail which he has been using to get away with his actions. This concludes with a notice of termination of Dr. Gables and the reassignment of the SCP project to another researcher.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The dynamics of the relationships between Foundation researchers as well as the covert workings of a researcher with their own agendas and goals.

Additional Notes: I'm scared that readers may lose interest before getting to the meat of the story which would take place in the experiment logs and other attached documents.

Genre (Optional): Horror (body horror)

Page Layout (Optional): Class, containment procedures, description, addenda (including a voiceover mp3 file with sound effects)

Elevator Pitch: Pregnant woman is found frozen in the arctic, torn in half, fetus missing. Top half of body is dead, lower half moves erratically on its own, possibly with a purpose or cognition.

Central Narrative: Corpse was found frozen in Yukon when villagers noticed a strange, unidentified creature moving erratically. Corpse's lower half is controlled by a series of live neurons that consume the bone and ligament tissue and shock the muscles into moving convulsively, allowing it to crawl. It will violently hyperextend its joints (bending knees backwards and such) and break its own bones to move.

+ show block
– hide block

The live neuron DNA matches the dead woman, whose brain is somewhat shrunken, or possibly her fetus. Lead scientist believes it's capable of navigation and is searching for something. During observation session, which is recorded as audio file, corpse's bottom half attempts to navigate the facility's halls and leave through the exit, which is locked, then scurries back to its top half in its freezer unit. As scientist closes the freezer door, listeners may hear the corpse vocalize its desire for its father, which is not written in transcript. Scientist does not hear it, dismissing it as his own involuntary vocalization. He regrets that the skip's lifespan is so short as a result of consuming its own flesh and progressively deflating in size, that they'll never know what it wants, so it must remain frozen to stay alive until the foundation finds a way to save it, find what it's looking for, or determine how it came to be.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Using body horror as a focus, of which I haven't seen much here, and a full story with open-ended conclusion that is coherent with beginning, middle, and end if the reader reads between the lines. Specifically, I'd like to include a voiceover file from the scientist's observation session with written transcript, recording the skittering and cracking noises the skip makes, with a subtle hint/easter egg for readers to listen for, revealing what it's capable of, and possibly answering the question of what it actually wants (this won't be included in the transcript, so that the reader is left to think and interpret it on their own).

Additional Notes: Please advise how to include the mp3 file with submission, as it's essential to the storytelling, thanks.

These objects are (but not limited to): manifestation of feelings described as "relaxation, peacefulness, etc.", diminished symptoms in subjects diagnosed with major depressive dissorder, etc. Objects interact with each other and are essential between themselves (For example: Access to XXXX-2 can only be done by interacting with XXXX-1, XXXX-3 is stored inside of XXXX-2 and any sample taken will disappear when
exiting XXXX-2)

Central Narrative: Discovered in a lab of an unknown GoI. Consists of an air freshener, a room that can only be accessed by smelling the content of the air freshener, and a lavender plant contained inside the room. The objects manifest anomalous anti-depressive and anti-memetic properties, since subjects exposed to any of the XXXX objects will manifest a general feeling of well-being; but they won't remember any initial exposition. Audiovisual data stored in a digital medium will experience total corruption and will be intelligible, however, textual and analogue data storage doesn't seem to be affected.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There's a fourth object which is only known to high clearance ranks. It's a virus that is presumably the cause of major depressive disorder and it's linked to the human subconscious since unknown times. Cannot be cured with any current means and it's symptoms can only be diminished with antidepressants. Also, one of the three initial objects has a very high value to the Foundation; it's a Thaumiel, and has a very high possibility to counterattack XXXX-4. Linked to SCP-5000 narrative (or at least I tried)

Additional Notes: I've started writing this SCP, but I would like to know if this idea hasn't been implemented. Also, I'm not a native english speaker, so sorri for may bed england.

item.content:encoded:

Genre (Optional): Comedy/Horror

Elevator Pitch: A Euclid SCP which creates instances of anomalous stone fountains in the yards of all integrated residents of a small, isolated township in Northern New Jersey. Memetic effects cause the population to consider the appearance and disappearance of these fountains as normal.

Central Narrative: The Foundation is in the process of investigating and researching this anomaly, but really no true containment is deemed necessary… so far. Researchers front as locals or vacationers to try and sneak past the defensive isolated population. Posing as an environmental group, they interview and interrogate locals on the appearance and disappearance of these fountains.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The memetic effects on the locals cause paranoia, defensiveness, and a stubborn attitude in regards to the fountains. This will be expanded upon in the interview logs, which I plan to have make up a lot of the page. Don't want to give TOO much away.
